summary.text: Chris Gober is the Republican nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Texas's 10th District. An attorney and business owner, he built a conservative election-law practice and in 2024 was director and chief lawyer of America PAC, a super PAC founded by Elon Musk that supported Donald Trump's presidential campaign. His campaign website describes him as the Trump-endorsed candidate and lists border security, opposing what it calls the weaponization of government, and economic growth among his priorities.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, he is a seventh-generation Texan who was born and raised in the Texas towns of Throckmorton and Graham, and he now lives in Austin with his wife and two daughters.
Graduated from Texas A&M University in 2001 and Harvard Law School in 2004.

Worked on national-security and border-security issues at the U.S. Department of Justice and then served as a top lawyer for the Republican Party, according to his campaign website; his Ballotpedia survey response places the party role with the Republican Party of Texas.
Founded a conservative law practice after returning to Texas. His campaign website says he started it with $10,000 in savings and that his businesses now employ more than 50 people across 17 states.

Says he represented conservative nonprofit groups in a case against the IRS over its tax-exempt rules and won a ruling striking down the regulation, and that he won a U.S. Supreme Court case for Sen. Ted Cruz challenging a provision of the Federal Election Campaign Act.

In 2024, served as director and chief lawyer of America PAC, which he says deployed nearly $300 million supporting Donald Trump's presidential campaign; he also says he defended the PAC and Elon Musk in lawsuits.

Says he helped establish the America First Policy Institute and helped deliver a Republican redistricting plan. He has not previously held elected office; he advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary.
